page.layout: One printed page: running text in one column at the top, then the Hebrew lines set as a block, then FINIS, then a woodcut vase below. No margin notes.

main_text.l: contra eum denunciaret. Ergo id juris sempiterni Papæ Romani, in
quosvis Reges absque mandato divino expresso exercere possunt.
Ille accepit mandatum à Deo. Hic nunquam accepit, nec est acceptarus
unquam. ℞. Ad Posterius. A summo Pontifice Vet. Test.
ad Romanum Papam claudicat consequentia. 2. Absurdum
est dicere authoritate Pontificia interfecisse Athaliam. Nam præter Sa-
cerdotium in Iojadah alia ratio etiam fuit, eaque gemina. 1. Quia
civis Regni fuit, at contra tyrannos, qui vi aperta Regnum oc-
cupant, civi liberum est insurgere. Pontifex autem Romanus,
armat & instruit se se contra eos, in quorum Regna nullum jus
habet. 2. Quia nulla ratio dari potest, quâ probari posset Atha-
liam Reginam fuisse legitimam, fuit enim alienigena, alienigenam
autem Reginam habere interdictum est, Deut.17.15.
מלך אשר יבחר יהוה אלהים בו מקרב אחיך תשים עליך מלך לא תוכל
לאת עליך איש נכרי אשר לא אחיך הוא

page.notes: The Hebrew block is printed in three lines and reads from right to left; the letters are copied as seen but the vowel points are not clear, so the Hebrew may contain small errors. Below FINIS is a woodcut of a footed vase full of flowers, not text. Faint show-through text from the reverse side is visible in the lower half and is not transcribed. The "℞." before "Ad Posterius" is a small printed mark within the line. The first word "contra" has a large initial letter.
